Frequently Asked Questions

Quick answers about booking, visits and costs.

01What happens at the first visit?

The first visit includes an examination and, where needed, digital x-rays. The findings are shown on screen, and treatment options and fees are explained before anything starts.

02Will I know the cost before treatment?

Yes. Fees are explained and agreed before treatment starts. Where a treatment has a fixed fee, it is listed on that treatment’s page.

03Can I use CHAS, MediSave or my Pioneer or Merdeka Generation card?

CHAS Blue and Orange, Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation cards are accepted for selected treatments. Bring the card and NRIC to registration. MediSave can be used for some surgical procedures, such as dental implants, within MOH limits.

04Can a dentist help with snoring?

A dentist screens for clinical signs that may suggest a sleep-related breathing disorder; we do not diagnose one. A formal diagnosis is made by an ENT surgeon or sleep physician, usually with a sleep study. Our role is to recognise the signs early, guide growth where appropriate, and refer to the right medical specialist. For adults diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnoea, a custom oral appliance is a recognised option, especially when CPAP is not tolerated (AASM and AADSM clinical guideline, 2015).

05My child breathes through the mouth or has crowded teeth. Where do I start?

A dental check looks at how the jaws are growing, the bite, and tongue and lip habits. Depending on the findings, options can include myofunctional therapy (delivered by partner speech therapists), aligners for growing children, or a referral to an ENT.

06Not sure which treatment fits?

Take the 60-second self-check above, or book a general check-up. The dentist explains which consultation to book next.

Sleep apnoea quiz for adults

A quick STOP-Bang screening for sleep apnoea. Results by email.

WhatsApp

What STOP-Bang asks

The first four questions are about sleep and health. The last four are about body size, age and gender, each linked to a higher likelihood of sleep apnoea.

STOP-Bang questionnaire: Chung et al., Anesthesiology, 2008

SSnoring
TTiredness
OObserved pauses
PBlood pressure
BBMI over 35
AAge over 50
NNeck size
GGender (male)

Signs of a breathing problem during sleep

In children, it often shows up as restlessness or poor focus, not tiredness.

  • Snoring most nights
  • Noisy breathing
  • Pauses in breathing
  • Bed-wetting
  • Mouth breathing
  • Morning headaches or dry mouth
  • Waking up tired
  • Sleepy in class
  • Fidgety or poor focus

Take the quiz

  1. SSnoring
  2. TTiredness
  3. OObserved
  4. PPressure
  5. BBMI
  6. AAge
  7. NNeck
  8. GGender
  1. Breathing at night1–6
  2. Mouth breathing, dry mouth, bed-wetting7–9
  3. Sleepiness and waking up10–14
  4. Growth and weight15–16
  5. Attention and behaviour17–22

What the score means

The score is the share of Yes answers among the questions answered Yes or No. Don’t know answers are left out. The cut-off, 0.33, is about one Yes in every three answers.

Lower risk
Higher risk
00.33 cut-off1

How it’s worked out

Yes answers ÷ (Yes + No answers)
8 Yes, 14 No8 ÷ 22 = 0.36Higher risk
  • Below 0.33, lower risk: a sleep-related breathing problem is less likely. Snoring on most nights, mouth breathing or daytime tiredness are still worth having checked.
  • 0.33 or above, higher risk: an assessment is the next step, which may include a referral to an ENT surgeon or sleep physician for a sleep study.

A higher score is not a diagnosis, and a lower score does not rule a problem out.

When snoring is worth checking

Occasional snoring, for example during a cold, is common in children. Snoring on more than half of nights, loud snoring, or pauses in breathing are worth having checked. Enlarged tonsils and adenoids, allergies and a blocked nose are common reasons for a child’s airway to narrow during sleep, and are assessed by an ENT surgeon.

What the score means

Each Yes scores 1 point, so the score runs from 0 to 8. The result email explains the score in more detail.

0 to 2Low risk
3 to 4Intermediate risk
5 to 8High risk
012345678
  • 0 to 2, low risk: moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnoea is less likely. Ongoing tiredness or poor sleep is still worth raising with a doctor or dentist.
  • 3 to 4, intermediate risk: an assessment is a sensible next step.
  • 5 to 8, high risk: moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnoea is more likely. An assessment and a sleep study are the usual next steps.

A high score is not a diagnosis, and a low score does not rule sleep apnoea out. Diagnosis needs a sleep study.

Questions about the sleep quiz

Is the quiz a diagnosis?

No. STOP-Bang screens for risk. Obstructive sleep apnoea is diagnosed by a sleep physician or ENT surgeon, usually with a sleep study.

Why does it ask about BMI, age, neck size and gender?

Each is linked to a higher likelihood of obstructive sleep apnoea, so the questionnaire counts them alongside the sleep questions.

What if no one has seen the breathing pauses?

Answer No if it isn’t known. A partner or family member can help with the snoring and breathing questions.

What if there’s already a sleep study?

The quiz isn’t needed. Book a consultation and bring the sleep study report.

What happens to the email and phone number?

They are used to send the result and for DP Dental to follow up about it. Details are in the privacy policy.

Is there a quiz for children?

Yes. The child sleep quiz is for ages 2 to 17 and is filled in by a parent or caregiver.

What happens next

The result is a starting point. A consultation looks at the answers alongside an examination, and a referral is made when a doctor needs to assess the child.

  1. 01

    Result by email

  2. 02

    Consultation

    The dentist goes through the answers, asks about the child’s sleep, and examines the teeth, jaw, tongue and breathing.

  3. 03

    Referral

    To an ENT surgeon or sleep physician when needed, who may arrange a sleep study.

  4. 04

    A plan agreed together

    With the child’s doctor, and dental care such as growth guidance or myofunctional therapy where appropriate.

Questions about the child sleep quiz

Is snoring normal in children?

Occasional snoring, for example during a cold, is common. Snoring on more than half of nights is worth having checked.

Who should fill in the quiz?

A parent or caregiver who knows how the child sleeps. Another adult who sees the child asleep, such as a grandparent or helper, can help with the night-time questions.

Why are there questions about attention and behaviour?

Poor sleep in children can show up as inattention, fidgeting or hyperactivity during the day, so the questionnaire includes them. They don’t diagnose ADHD or any other condition.

Does a higher score mean the child has sleep apnoea?

No. It means an assessment is worth doing. A diagnosis needs a sleep study arranged by a doctor.

What age is the quiz for?

Children aged 2 to 17. For 18 and over, there is the adult sleep quiz.

What does treatment for children involve?

It depends on the cause and is planned with the child’s doctor. Enlarged tonsils or adenoids are managed by an ENT surgeon. Dental care can include growth guidance and myofunctional therapy where appropriate.

What happens to the email and phone number?

They are used to send the result and for DP Dental to follow up about it. Details are in the privacy policy.

Services Smartee Clear Aligners

Smartee Clear Aligners in Singapore

Clear, removable aligners for children, teenagers and adults, planned around the bite and jaw, with myofunctional exercises where needed.

WhatsApp

What Smartee aligners are

Smartee aligners are a series of clear, removable plastic trays made for one patient’s teeth. Each set is worn for a set period, then replaced by the next, moving the teeth a small step at a time. A dentist plans the treatment and reviews it throughout.

  • Clear and removable
  • Taken out to eat, brush and floss
  • Made for one patient’s teeth from their dental records
  • Planned and reviewed by a dentist at the clinic
2004Making clear aligners since
1.6M+Smiles treated, as reported by Smartee
44Countries

Who clear aligners are for

Clear aligners are used for a range of alignment and bite problems. Whether they suit a particular case is decided at a consultation.

  • 01
    Crowded teeth
  • 02
    Gaps between teeth
  • 03
    Overbite, underbite or crossbite
  • 04
    Teeth that have moved after earlier braces
  • 05
    Children whose jaws are still growing
  • 06
    Cases where removing teeth was suggested, planned with minimal extraction where clinically suitable

Options for children, teenagers and adults

Children

Smartee KINDER (ages 3 to 10) where straightening the teeth is the whole goal. Smartee AG KIDS (ages 3 to 16) where jaw growth and habits also need guiding.

Teenagers

Smartee TEEN, for teenagers whose treatment goal is straightening the teeth.

Adults

Smartee GE for straightening the teeth, and Smartee GS where the bite and jaw relationship also needs correcting, planned to minimise or avoid extractions and jaw surgery where clinically suitable.

Growth guidance for children

How the lips, tongue and breathing work at rest shapes how a child’s jaws and teeth develop. Smartee AG KIDS works on all three.

Questions, answered.

Still unsure?

Talk to the team at DP Dental Orchard by phone or WhatsApp.

Call 6219 3082 WhatsApp
How much does Smartee treatment cost?

The fee depends on the option a case needs and is confirmed after a consultation.

How long does treatment take?

It depends on how far the teeth need to move and, for children, on growth. The dentist gives an estimate at the consultation.

How many hours a day are aligners worn?

Most of the day and night, usually 20 to 22 hours. They are taken out to eat, to drink anything other than water, and to brush.

Will teeth need to be removed?

Treatment is planned with minimal extraction where clinically suitable. Whether any tooth needs removing is decided at the consultation.

Will the teeth move back after treatment?

Teeth can move after any orthodontic treatment. Retainers are worn afterwards to hold them in place.

Why start while a child is still growing?

While the jaws are still growing, treatment can guide how they develop as well as straighten the teeth. Whether starting early suits a particular child is decided at a consultation.

Can aligners treat snoring or sleep apnoea?

No. Snoring and breathing concerns need assessment by an ENT surgeon or sleep physician. Dental treatment can run alongside that assessment. See Sleep Apnoea & Snoring.

Is treatment reviewed in person?

Yes. Every stage is planned and reviewed at the clinic by a dentist.

Services Sleep Apnoea & Snoring

Snoring and sleep apnoea

Sleep Apnoea and Snoring Treatment in Singapore

Screening, referral and custom oral appliances for snoring and obstructive sleep apnoea, working with ENT surgeons and sleep physicians.

WhatsApp
On CPAP? See the options →

Overview

What obstructive sleep apnoea is

During sleep, the muscles of the throat relax. In obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), the airway narrows or closes for short periods, so breathing stops and starts through the night. Each time, the brain briefly wakes the body to reopen the airway, usually too briefly to remember. This breaks up sleep.

1 in 3adults in a Singapore community study had moderate to severe sleep-disordered breathing.Tan et al., Respirology, 2016

A two-minute sleep check

Snoring and daytime tiredness are common, and they're often noticed by a partner before the person themselves. The STOP-Bang questionnaire is a short screening tool used by doctors and dentists to gauge the likelihood of obstructive sleep apnoea.Snoring and daytime tiredness are often noticed by a partner first.

  • Eight yes-or-no questions, about two minutes

  • The result is sent by email once the last question is answered

Who is the sleep check for?

Takes about 2 minutesA screening check, not a diagnosisBased on the STOP-Bang questionnaire for adults and the Pediatric Sleep Questionnaire for children.

Breathing paused · 0s

That's what an apnoea looks like. Check if it's happening to you.

Signs

Common signs of sleep apnoea

Many people with sleep apnoea don’t notice the pauses in their breathing. A partner or family member notices first.

  • Loud, regular snoring
  • Pauses in breathing, or gasping or choking during sleep
  • Waking up tired after a full night’s sleep
  • Sleepiness during the day
  • Morning headaches
  • Poor concentration
  • Several trips to the bathroom at night

Treatment

Treatment options

Oral appliance

A custom appliance worn during sleep that holds the lower jaw slightly forward, designed to keep the airway more open. Used alongside the care of a sleep physician.

Myofunctional therapy

Exercises for tongue posture, lip seal and nasal breathing, used alongside other treatment.

Learn More →

For children

Growth guidance and myofunctional care for children with jaw development needs, alongside a referral to an ENT surgeon or sleep physician.

Learn More →

How the appliance works

Moving the jaw forward to open the airway

The tongue is attached to the lower jaw. When the lower jaw sits slightly further forward during sleep, the tongue comes forward with it, leaving more room in the airway behind it. Drag the slider to move the jaw.

Adjusted in small steps

  1. 1

    Measured

    The jaw muscles are relaxed and the bite is recorded before the appliance is made.

  2. 2

    Fitted

    The appliance is fitted at a starting position.

  3. 3

    Adjusted

    It is moved forward in small steps over several weeks, with the jaw and bite checked along the way.

  4. 4

    Checked

    A follow-up sleep study with the sleep physician checks how the appliance is working.

The jaw is moved forward gradually so the jaw joints and muscles can be checked at each step.

Finding CPAP hard?

CPAP is a common first treatment for obstructive sleep apnoea, and some people find it hard to keep using. For adults with obstructive sleep apnoea who cannot tolerate CPAP or prefer another option, clinical guidelines list a custom oral appliance as a treatment to consider, alongside the care of a sleep physician.

CPAP compared with a custom oral appliance
CPAPCustom oral appliance
How it worksA machine blows air through a mask to keep the airway open.Holds the lower jaw slightly forward during sleep, designed to keep the airway more open.
What is wornA mask over the nose, or nose and mouth, joined to the machine by a hose.A custom appliance over the teeth.
PowerNeeds a power supply.No power needed.
TravelThe machine, mask and hose travel together.Fits in a small case.
Who is involvedPrescribed and reviewed by the sleep physician.Made by the dentist after a diagnosis from an ENT surgeon or sleep physician. A follow-up sleep study checks how it is working.

Using both

Some people use an oral appliance together with CPAP, or keep the appliance for travel, as agreed with the sleep physician.

Already diagnosed and finding CPAP hard? The options can be discussed at a consultation. CPAP should not be stopped without speaking to the sleep physician.

Questions about sleep apnoea treatment

Still unsure?

Talk to the team at DP Dental Orchard by phone or WhatsApp.

Call 6219 3082 WhatsApp
Is a sleep study needed first?

The diagnosis comes from a sleep study arranged by a sleep physician or ENT surgeon. If there isn’t one yet, a referral is made at the consultation.

Does snoring mean sleep apnoea?

Not always. Snoring is common, and not everyone who snores has sleep apnoea. Loud snoring with pauses in breathing, gasping or daytime sleepiness is a reason to be checked. Only a sleep study can tell.

Does an oral appliance change the bite?

Some people notice changes in how their teeth meet over time, so the bite is checked at review visits.

How long before it is working?

The appliance is moved forward in small steps over several weeks. A follow-up sleep study with the sleep physician then checks how it is working.

Can children have sleep apnoea?

Yes. Signs in children can include snoring, mouth breathing, restless sleep, bed-wetting, and tiredness or hyperactivity during the day. The Child Sleep Quiz is a starting point; a doctor makes the diagnosis.

Is treatment covered by insurance or Medisave?

      Overview

      Common symptoms

        In pain now

        Toothache now?

        Toothache that lasts more than two days, or doesn’t ease with pain relief, needs a dental check. The cause is found with an exam and X-rays.

        Go to A&E, or call 995, if there is:

        • Swelling around the eye or down the neck
        • Swelling that makes it hard to breathe, swallow or speak
        • Difficulty opening the mouth
        • A swollen or painful eye, or sudden problems with eyesight

        Ask someone else to drive, or call 995 for an ambulance.

        Getting seen

        Call or WhatsApp DP Dental Orchard for the earliest appointment.

        Mon to Fri
        9 am to 6 pm
        Sat
        9 am to 5 pm
        Sun
        Closed
        Call 6219 3082 WhatsApp

        Until the appointment

        • Pain relief from a pharmacy, taken as the pack directs. A pharmacist can advise.

          Children under 16 should not take aspirin.

        • Soft foods, chewing on the other side.

        • Avoiding food and drinks that are very hot, very cold or sweet.

        • For adults: a rinse with half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water, spat out afterwards.

          Not for children.

        Source: NHS, Toothache (reviewed July 2024) and Dental abscess (reviewed March 2026).

        Signs

          How the joint works

          Why the jaw clicks

          Each jaw joint has a small disc of cartilage between the rounded top of the lower jaw and the skull. The disc moves with the jaw every time the mouth opens and closes. Choose a state to see what happens to the disc.

          Based on the Diagnostic Criteria for TMD (Schiffman et al., J Oral Facial Pain Headache, 2014). Illustration simplified for education.

          Disc in place

          The disc stays on top of the jaw bone as the jaw opens and closes, so the movement is smooth and quiet.

          Clicking

          The disc has slipped slightly forward. As the mouth opens, the jaw bone moves forward and slides back under the disc, which makes the click. As the mouth closes, the disc can slip forward again, sometimes with a second, softer click.

          Locking

          The disc stays in front of the jaw bone and does not slip back. It can block the jaw from moving forward, so the mouth does not open fully. Clicking that stops, followed by opening that becomes limited, can be a sign of this.

          A click on its own, with no pain and no change in opening, is common. An examination is recommended when clicking comes with pain, when the jaw catches or locks, or when the mouth does not open fully.

            About Us

            Gentle, honest dentistry — for the whole family

            We're a team of dentists and care staff who believe a visit to the dentist should feel easy. That means clear advice, fair pricing, and the time to answer every question.

            Our story

            DP Dental started in 2006 as a small practice with one dental chair. Today we’re a boutique practice with two clinics in Orchard and Katong, eight chairs and a team of more than 40 people — providing ethical, evidence-based dentistry with an integrative, functional approach.

            We travel the world for up-to-date knowledge and skills, so we can solve problems at the root cause with the best minimally invasive options. Our Mandarin name, 诚芯牙医, sums up how we work: honest dentistry with a heart.

            “We only prescribe for our patients what we would for our own family members.”

            What we stand for

            Three promises we make to every patient who walks through our door.

            01

            Comfort first

            Gentle techniques, clear explanations and no rushing — so even nervous patients feel at ease in the chair.

            02

            Honest pricing

            Every treatment is priced up front, with schemes like CHAS, Medisave and Baby Bonus accepted where eligible.

            03

            Care for every age

            From a child’s first check-up to implants and sleep care later in life — one team that knows your family’s history.

            Sustainability

            The first B Corp certified dental practice in Singapore and Asia

            Looking after people and the planet is part of how we run every clinic. Our core values come down to three things: people, purpose and planet.

            What B Corp means

            B Corp certification measures a business on more than profit. B Lab looks at five areas: governance, workers, customers, community and the environment. To keep the certification, we have to meet its standards for social and environmental performance, transparency and accountability.

            Dentistry uses a lot of materials, energy, chemicals and water, and produces a lot of waste. With Singapore aiming for net zero by 2050, we want to show that high-quality care doesn't have to cost the environment.

            Certified since November 2023 · Medical & dental practice · Singapore

            View our B Lab directory listing

            Three pillars

            How our sustainability work shows up day to day.

            Planet

            We focus on prevention, which cuts down on costly treatment and its environmental footprint. Patient records are digital to save paper, and we're phasing out single-use plastic in our clinics. We've signed the UN Global Compact's Pledge for the Planet and are working out what it will take to become a Net Zero business.

            People

            We were one of the first companies in Singapore to move to a 4-day work week with no change in salary. We won the Learning Enterprise Alliance Award in 2021, and DP Healthverse is Great Place to Work® certified for 2024.

            Community

            We received the Company of Good – 3 Hearts recognition in 2024 for our corporate purpose and community impact. We also run oral-health awareness work so more people catch problems early.
